title: bug: protected standalone moe-call.sh direct execution runs a project bash through its env shebang before PATH scrubbing
description:
Adversarial review of task-0b2ea570: moe-call.sh still starts with #!/usr/bin/env bash. From a scratch project containing executable ./bash, direct exec with MOE_RUNTIME_PROTECTED=1 and PATH=.:/usr/bin:/bin runs that plant before the script body (exit 42, ran.log='project bash').
Reproduced on the final task worktree bytes; fixture at /mnt/d/moe-scratch/0b2ea570-work/residuals-xhs0e985. Current approved M2 rows invoke /bin/bash explicitly and cannot cover kernel/env interpreter selection.
Keep this separate from the approved PATH-body scrub; add direct-exec coverage and define a trusted interpreter entry path without changing legacy behavior.
definitionOfDone: Under MOE_RUNTIME_PROTECTED=1, supported direct invocation cannot select a project bash before the helper body; add a non-vacuous planted-bash regression.
Preserve supported Linux/macOS/Git Bash entry behavior and legacy compatibility; document any direct-invocation limitation.

'PATH=".:$PATH"; export PATH; ' : '') + 'exec "$0" "$@"', shellPath(layout.helper), 'get_context', '{}', '--project', shellPath(project)], { cwd: project, env, timeout: 20_000 }). The shim only sets PATH and execs the file by path, so the kernel (or MSYS on Windows) reads the shebang: this is real direct execution.
- With `via` (POSIX only): spawnSync(via, [layout.helper, 'get_context', '{}', '--project', project]) with a '.'-first PATH.

implementationPlan.description:
Implementation. Edit scripts/moe-call.sh only, in place, with the Edit tool. Keep mode 100755, LF line endings, and the body below the new block byte-identical.

Line 1 becomes `#!/bin/sh`: the kernel (or MSYS) starts a fixed path, so no PATH entry chooses the interpreter. After the usage header and before `set -euo pipefail` (:13), insert a comment of at most 6 lines. It says why (task-0d9ebe5b), that the legacy hand-over keeps the old PATH lookup, and that MOE_CALL_BASH_ENTRY allows one hand-over. Then insert this block. It was prototyped and passed on dash, bash-as-sh, POSIXLY_CORRECT and Git Bash; the artifacts are in /mnt/d/moe-scratch/0d9ebe5b-arch.

if [ -z "${MOE_CALL_BASH_ENTRY:-}" ]; then
    if [ -z "${BASH_VERSION:-}" ] || case ":${SHELLOPTS:-}:" in *:posix:*) true ;; *) false ;; esac; then
        MOE_CALL_BASH_ENTRY=1; export MOE_CALL_BASH_ENTRY
        if [ "${MOE_RUNTIME_PROTECTED:-}" = 1 ]; then
            [ -x /bin/bash ] || { echo "Error: MOE_PROTECTED_INTERPRETER_NOT_FOUND: /bin/bash is not executable; under MOE_RUNTIME_PROTECTED=1 run moe-call.sh as '<absolute path to bash> moe-call.sh'. Refusing to start." >&2; exit 1; }
            exec /bin/bash "$0" "$@"
        fi
        exec bash "$0" "$@"
    fi
fi
unset MOE_CALL_BASH_ENTRY
[ -n "${BASH_VERSION:-}" ] || { echo "Error: moe-call.sh must run under bash; refusing to start." >&2; exit 1; }

Rules:
- Before bash runs, use builtins only: [, case, true, false, echo, export, unset, exec, exit. Under dash any other word, even `shopt`, is a PATH lookup that a project file could answer. So detect POSIX mode from SHELLOPTS (bash lists posix there when it runs as sh or under POSIXLY_CORRECT), never with shopt.
- Under the marker, the only interpreters are /bin/sh and /bin/bash, with no fallback to `bash` by PATH.
- Legacy keeps `bash` by PATH, exactly as `#!/usr/bin/env bash` did, with the same argv shape (`bash <script path> args`). So BASH_SOURCE and find_proxy are unchanged.
- A non-POSIX-mode bash skips the block: no extra exec and unchanged behavior. That covers every `bash moe-call.sh` caller: the moe-agent.sh deregisters, the MOE_FALLBACK_CLI prompt, claudeHook.ts and baselineRun.ts.
- The sentinel allows exactly one hand-over. A bash that still starts in POSIX mode (POSIXLY_CORRECT) then runs the body as the old shebang did and never loops. It is unset before the body, so node and the proxy never inherit it.
- Error handling: the /bin/bash refusal, and the final bash check for a forged sentinel or a PATH `bash` that is not bash. So the body never runs in another shell.

Check that `bash -n scripts/moe-call.sh` passes. `dash -n` fails on the body's here-string by design: dash runs commands one at a time and execs before it reaches the body.
implementationPlan.note: Line 1 is now #!/bin/sh; a 5-line comment plus the plan's builtins-only hand-over block sit before `set -euo pipefail` (sentinel MOE_CALL_BASH_ENTRY, /bin/bash under the exact marker with MOE_PROTECTED_INTERPRETER_NOT_FOUND refusal, legacy `exec bash`, unset, final bash check). executionContract.intendedBehavior:
Run by path, scripts/moe-call.sh starts under /bin/sh. Using shell builtins only, it hands itself to bash once:
- under MOE_RUNTIME_PROTECTED=1, to exactly /bin/bash, refusing with MOE_PROTECTED_INTERPRETER_NOT_FOUND when that file is not executable;
- otherwise, to `bash` by PATH lookup, as the old `#!/usr/bin/env bash` did.
Under the marker, a project file named bash or sh on a '.', relative or in-project PATH entry never runs. A caller that runs `bash moe-call.sh` in a non-POSIX-mode bash sees no change.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
1) `#!/bin/bash`: one line, and it matches moe-agent.sh's own shebang. Rejected: legacy direct exec would stop resolving bash by PATH (Homebrew bash on macOS), and hosts without /bin/bash (NixOS, BSD) would lose direct exec. That contradicts the row's 'without changing legacy behavior' and the established legacy-half pattern (W1/M2 assert that legacy still reaches the PATH lookup).
2) A guard in the body: impossible, because the shebang's interpreter runs before any body line.
3) A POSIX-sh scan of trusted PATH directories for bash under the marker: rejected. It needs the project path, so the argument parsing would be duplicated in sh, plus a second scanner. /bin/bash is the fixed system bash that moe-agent.sh's shebang already uses.
4) Always re-exec, with no POSIX-mode detection: rejected. It adds an exec and changes the interpreter for every explicit `bash moe-call.sh` caller.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
- Every Moe caller runs `bash moe-call.sh` explicitly: moe-agent.sh's two deregisters (after its PATH scrub), the MOE_FALLBACK_CLI prompt, packages/moe-daemon/src/util/claudeHook.ts and benchmarks/baselineRun.ts. Only humans and agents running it by path go through the shebang, as the docs show (`scripts/moe-call.sh get_context ...`).
- /bin/sh here is dash, with no BASH_VERSION. On macOS, Fedora and Git Bash, /bin/sh is bash in POSIX mode: SHELLOPTS then contains posix. Verified here with a sh->bash symlink and with POSIXLY_CORRECT=1.
- macOS /bin/sh also has xpg_echo, which would mangle `echo "$REQUEST"` JSON. So the body must never run in a POSIX-mode sh, and that is why the hand-over is needed rather than tolerated.
- The prototype ran green: dash and bash-as-sh under both marker and legacy, POSIXLY_CORRECT with no loop, explicit bash unchanged, a forged sentinel refused, and a PATH bash that is really dash refused. Windows Node plus Git Bash direct exec of TEMP copies passed too: new bytes refuse the plant, old bytes run it. Artifacts: /mnt/d/moe-scratch/0d9ebe5b-arch (winprobe.mjs, orig.sh, the prototype moe-call.sh).
- Read mem:gotcha-protected-moe-call-direct-exec-shebang and mem:gotcha-protected-interpreter-pin (the QA RED recipe and sh mutation tips).
planningNotes.risks:
(a) A POSIX-mode bash must hand over, but only once. With POSIXLY_CORRECT, a missing sentinel means an infinite exec loop; D3 catches it.
(b) Under dash, any non-builtin word in the block is a PATH lookup.
(c) Windows cannot exec a shebang script, so the Windows rows go through a Git Bash -c shim. MSYS treats `#!` files as executable (verified with Windows Node and TEMP copies).
(d) A host with /tmp mounted noexec would fail the direct-exec rows. The existing harness already execs stubs from tmpdir.
(e) `dash -n scripts/moe-call.sh` fails by design: do not add it to any gate.
(f) The ps1 twin task-3acf7f79 also edited this ARCHITECTURE bullet; it is DONE and a declared dependency.
